nodes.name: PVA-CS-Borax Hydrogel Formation
nodes.procedure: The carbon fiber paper (CFP) was first dipped into a solution of polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and chitosan (CS), crosslinked with borax.

nodes.procedure: then immersed in a POMs ([Mo7O24]6-, denoted as Mo7) solution to absorb Mo7 POMs through the electrostatic interaction of ammonium groups from chitosan and the anionic Mo7 POMs.

nodes.name: Pyrolysis to Mo2C/CFP
nodes.procedure: The resulting material was pyrolyzed at 800 °C to form the desired porous Mo2C doped carbon aerogel on CFP (denoted as Mo2C/CFP).

nodes.name: Pt Electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Subsequently, the target Pt@Mo2C/CFP electrocatalyst was prepared by the electrodeposition of Pt using 1.0 M KOH solution that contained [PtCl6]2-. The optimal conditions for Pt electrodeposition are established as 400 cyclic voltammetry cycles exerted within the potential range of 0 and -0.50 V (vs. RHE) in a [PtCl6]2- solution with a controlled concentration of 60 μM.

nodes.description: HER performance in 1.0 M KOH three-electrode system
nodes.source_text: Figure 4A demonstrates that the Pt@Mo₂C/CFP electrocatalyst has the highest HER activity. Specifically, the Pt@Mo₂C/CFP electrocatalyst demands rather low overpotential of 17±3.2 and 127±6.8 mV at 10 and 100 mA cm⁻², respectively... The Pt@Mo₂C/CFP carbon aerogel catalyst demonstrates exceptional durability in alkaline media, sustaining HER for 500 h @ 10 mA cm-2 and 250 h @ 100 mA cm-2 in 1.0 M KOH

nodes.description: Alkaline water electrolyzer performance with NiFe LDH anode
nodes.source_text: the as-prepared self-supporting Pt@Mo₂C/CFP electrocatalyst was utilized for the cathode in a single cell alkaline electrolyzer... The Pt@Mo₂C/CFP cathode and the NiFe LDH anode are tightly pressed on both sides of ZrO₂-modified polyphenylene sulfite (PPS) membrane... needs 2.1 V to reach 1.0 A cm⁻², or 2.4 V to achieve a current density of 2.0 A cm⁻²... long-projected lifetime over 100 h at 60 °C under a high current density of 500 mA cm⁻²

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM reveals continuously porous network structure of Pt@Mo2C/CFP and Mo2C/CFP aerogels.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) was utilized to study morphology of Mo2C/CFP aerogel (Fig. S1), revealing continuously porous network structure... The porous network structure retained within the Pt@Mo2C/CFP carbon aerogel after electrodeposition (Fig. 2A).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows nanoparticles in Pt@Mo2C/CFP have an average size of 3.69 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscopy (TEM) shows that nanoparticles have an average size of 3.69 nm (Fig. 2B).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice fringes of 0.227 nm (Pt (111)) and 0.228 nm (Mo2C (121)) in Pt@Mo2C/CFP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM (HRTEM) images of Pt@Mo2C/CFP in Fig. 2C demonstrated two sets of lattice fringes with distances spacing measuring 0.227 and 0.228 nm. These values, respectively, corresponded to the (111) plane of Pt and (121) plane of Mo2C.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM shows single Pt atoms, Pt clusters and Pt NPs co-existing in Pt@Mo2C/CFP carbon aerogel.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To further identify the distribution of Pt on Pt@Mo2C/CFP carbon aerogel catalyst, we obtained the aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) (Fig. 2D), which indicate single Pt atoms, Pt clusters and Pt NPs co-existed...

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mappings confirm Mo and Pt elements evenly distributed in Pt@Mo2C/CFP with similar intensities.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) mappings further confirmed that Mo and Pt elements are evenly distributed within the Pt@Mo2C/CFP carbon aerogel electrocatalyst (Fig. 2E). Notably, the intensity of Pt closely approximates that of the Mo element...

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS shows Pt content of ~0.05 wt% (~0.03 mg cm^-2) in Pt@Mo2C/CFP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The amount of Pt in the Pt@Mo2C/CFP was tested via inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and found to be around 0.05 wt% (~0.03 mg cm^-2) in Table S1.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows characteristic diffraction peaks of Pt (PDF No. 88-2343), Mo2C (PDF No. 79-0744) and graphite carbon (PDF No. 75-1621) in Pt@Mo2C/CFP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XRD patterns of Pt@Mo2C/CFP electrocatalyst displayed the characteristic diffraction peaks of Pt (Pt, PDF No. 88-2343), Mo2C (Mo2C, PDF No. 79-0744) and graphite carbon (C, PDF No. 75-1621) (Fig. S3)...

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS survey shows presence of Mo, Pt, C, O, N elements. C 1s: sp2-C (284.4 eV), sp3-C (285.1 eV), C-N/C-O (286.5 eV), C=O (288.5 eV). N 1s: pyridine-N (398.3 eV), pyrrolic-N (400.2 eV), graphitic-N (401.6 eV). Mo 3d in Pt@Mo2C/CFP: Mo6+ (232.4/235.5 eV), Mo4+ (230.7/233.9 eV); Mo2+ (228.5/231.6 eV) only in Mo2C/CFP. Pt 4f: Pt0 (71.2/74.5 eV), oxidized Pt (72.5/75.8 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS survey spectrum in Fig. 3A demonstrates the Mo, Pt, C, O and N elements are present. As demonstrated in Fig. 3B, C 1s XPS spectra... In Fig. 3D, we attribute the peak at 232.4 and 235.5 eV to Mo6+... The high-resolution Pt 4f XPS spectrum in Fig. 3E shows...

nodes.characterization_summary: Contact angle testing shows electrochemical deposition of Pt improves hydrophilicity of Mo2C carbon aerogel.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Surface-wetting characterization using contact-angle testing shows that the electrochemical deposition of Pt significantly improves the interfacial hydrophilicity of Mo2C carbon aerogel electrocatalyst (Fig. 3F)...

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance Cdl of Pt@Mo2C/CFP is 32.8 mF cm^-2 (higher ECSA), Pt/CFP is 27.1 mF cm^-2, Mo2C/CFP is 21.5 mF cm^-2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To determine the electrochemically active specific surface area (ECSA) of the catalysts, double-layer capacitance (Cdl) analysis was carried out. As shown in Fig. S8, Cdl of Pt@Mo2C/CFP catalysts is 32.8 mF cm^-2, surpassing those of Pt/CFP (27.1 mF cm^-2) and Mo2C/CFP (21.5 mF cm^-2)...

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows low charge transfer resistance Rct = 2.64 Ω for Pt@Mo2C/CFP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) of Pt@Mo2C/CFP electrocatalyst further demonstrates its fast charge transfer behavior and low charge transfer resistance (Rct = 2.64 Ω).
